title: Worker payment distribution can be visible without restored worker power
source_unit: Federal Trade Commission Amazon Flex tip-refund program and eligible delivery drivers; named enforcement and refund-administration records, not a representative worker sample
geography: United States federal consumer-protection enforcement and eligible Amazon Flex drivers

observations.period: 2016 through August 2019 practice; payment administration checked September 17, 2026

current_reissue_route.value: Zelle payments to eligible drivers who did not cash their checks

continued_work_switching_household_recov.value: not observed in public refund record

observations.method: FTC official consent-order, payment-distribution announcement, and current refund-administration page; reported program terms and distribution stages are retained without treating them as a worker-level estimate.
observations.uncertainty: The current page does not publish the complete eligible-driver denominator, current-round success rate, individual amounts, failed delivery, remaining loss, continued work, alternative work, household recovery, or bargaining outcome. The formal amount and distribution total are not interchangeable.
observations.subgroup: Amazon Flex drivers eligible under the FTC refund program; earlier paid, uncashed, reissued, ineligible, and unknown-status drivers are distinct groups.
observations.counterinterpretation: Payment receipt may resolve a financial loss for some drivers without changing continued platform use or exit; failure to cash an earlier check may reflect address or payment-channel friction rather than refusal of the remedy.

related_sources.claim: FTC consent-order amount and future pay/tip disclosure and consent requirements.
FTC reported initial check and PayPal distribution counts and amounts.

boundary: This record establishes administrator-reported worker payment distribution and a current reissue route. It does not establish individual receipt, average recovery, remaining loss, continued work, alternative work, household security, bargaining power, trust, collective action, or exit. It is not a representative worker trend or a causal estimate.
